Assessment of the "Trump could strike Iran tomorrow" claim against approved sources. Iran International live blog, 24 October 2026, with timestamped entries at Oct 25, 2026, 06:56 GMT+0 and 05:49 GMT+0. Cross-checked against Al Jazeera, BBC, Times of Israel, CBS and CNBC. Compiled 08:50 GMT Sun 25 Oct 2026.

THE UNDERLYING CLAIM, AS IRAN INTERNATIONAL PUTS IT
- "President Donald Trump said the United States could strike Iran as soon as 'tomorrow' or reach an agreement with the Islamic Republic, adding he wanted a permanent solution to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon."
- Note that Iran International places "tomorrow" in quotation marks but supplies NO venue, NO time and NO surrounding verbatim sentence. It is a paraphrase with a single quoted word.
- Iran International's other escalation lines are sourced to outlets NOT on our approved list: "The Hill reported Saturday, citing two sources familiar with the planning" for post-midterm strike options; "The Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday" for munitions being loaded aboard the USS George Washington carrier strike group; "Axios said" on assassination-plot intelligence. The Hill and Axios are not approved. WSJ is approved but unreachable, so I could not verify it directly.

IS IT CARRIED BY AN APPROVED NON-IRAN-INTERNATIONAL SOURCE? YES, BUT ONLY AS FRAMING, NOT AS A QUOTE
- Al Jazeera, approved, live blog 25 Oct 2026: headline "Iran war live: Trump hints at possible Sunday Iran attack or deal reached", body: "US President Donald Trump says the US is considering a possible attack on Iran as soon as Sunday, pointing out that Washington might have to 'finish the job' or could reach a deal with Tehran." So Al Jazeera independently carries the Sunday framing. The claim is therefore not Iran International's alone.
- CRUCIALLY, the quoted fragment Al Jazeera attributes to Trump is "finish the job" — not "tomorrow" and not "Sunday". The date is Al Jazeera's construction, exactly as it is Iran International's.

THE ACTUAL VERBATIM TRUMP QUOTES, FROM APPROVED SOURCES — NEITHER CONTAINS A DATE
- BBC, datePublished 2026-10-24T21:12:55Z, dateModified 2026-10-25T02:27:15Z, asked about the war earlier on Saturday: "I've done it very effectively and I may have to finish it off, or maybe they'll make a deal, but I'm not sure. Either way, we win."
- Times of Israel live blog entry, 25 October 2026, 12:43 am Israel time = 21:43 GMT Sat 24 Oct: "Do you really think I'm going to tell you if I'm going to do it?" Trump responded when asked about the possibility of attacking Iran. He continued: "There's a possibility I will. There's also a possibility we'll have a nice, big, beautiful agreement."
- CBS News, October 23, 2026 / 11:13 PM EDT = 03:13 GMT 24 Oct, at a campaign rally in Florida on Friday: "We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree." Epic Fury is the codename of the US-Israel campaign launched on 28 February.

EVIDENCE POINTING THE OTHER WAY — THE PLANNING IS DOCUMENTED FOR AFTER 3 NOVEMBER, NOT TOMORROW
- Times of Israel: "The article notes that Trump had recently stated on social media he would not strike Iran before the November 3 midterm elections."
- CNBC, 24 Oct 2026: "The Trump administration has vowed to put off military strikes on Iran after the midterm elections on Nov. 3."
- CBS, 23 Oct: "President Trump has not ruled out restarting hostilities after next month's midterm elections."
- Al Jazeera, 24 Oct, citing the New York Times (approved): "the US and Israel have drafted plans for a campaign of attacks on Iran that would take place AFTER the US midterm elections on November 3", describing intensified drills for "a short but intensive operation", with potential targets including Iran's "energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and missile and drone arsenal".
- Iran International's own entry says US Central Command has follow-up strike plans ready "after November's midterm elections", which contradicts its own "tomorrow" line.

VERDICT: THIS IS ONE OFFICIAL'S RHETORIC, NOT A DEVELOPMENT
Trump was asked whether he would attack Iran and pointedly refused to say ("Do you really think I'm going to tell you if I'm going to do it?"). Two outlets, Iran International and Al Jazeera, converted that refusal plus "I may have to finish it off" into a specific date. No approved source has Trump uttering "tomorrow" or "Sunday". Every piece of documented planning in approved sources — NYT via Al Jazeera, CNBC, CBS, and Iran International's own CENTCOM line — points to AFTER 3 November, and Trump himself said on social media he would not strike before the midterms. RECOMMENDATION: do not run this as an imminent-strike item. If the Iran posture is used at all, use the verbatim refusal and the post-midterm planning, and state the contradiction.

WHAT IS GENUINELY SOLID ON IRAN TODAY (two-source, named officials)
- Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, in an unclassified memo to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday: Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel" abroad and "The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries." CIA Director John Ratcliffe was copied. Carried by CBS (23 Oct, 11:13 PM EDT = 03:13 GMT 24 Oct), NBC (Oct. 24, 2026, 7:49 AM EDT = 11:49 GMT 24 Oct, byline Abigail Williams and Freddie Clayton) and CNBC (24 Oct). The memo does not identify specific targets or countries, or say whether attacks may be imminent. Axios first reported it.
- Times of Israel live blog, 7:34 AM Israel time = 05:34 GMT today: two senior Iranian officials, one an IRGC member, confirmed to the New York Times that Tehran is preparing to target US diplomats and personnel, saying the targeting of American officials was considered "fair game" given Iranian officials killed by the US and Israel. A US official reported evidence of Iranian operatives in the US who are "not just simply Iranian nationals." This is an ADVANCE on the DNI memo: Iranian officials themselves now confirming intent.
- State Department has ordered non-essential embassy personnel and families to depart Saudi Arabia ("ordered departure", announced Wednesday); multiple posts including Lebanon, UAE, Qatar and Jordan on "restricted operations" status. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott on X: "The safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority."
- Iranian Armed Forces Chief of Staff Ali Abdollahi, Saturday: the US military would not be allowed in the Gulf "under any circumstances and at any time", adding Trump could only "dream" of seeing US forces enter the Gulf and would take his dream to the grave (Al Jazeera). CBS World index carried "Iran says U.S. military not allowed in Gulf 'under any circumstance'" updated approximately 07:40 GMT today.
- Iranian government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani, Saturday: Tehran would not "wait for permission to defend itself"; "Our position is clear: we do not flee from dialogue for peace, and we do not hesitate in defending the country. Those who harbour the illusion of destroying Iran must correct their calculations."
- Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian blamed Washington for the unravelling of the interim deal but said both sides should return to it and "conclude it" (Press TV via Al Jazeera, Saturday).
- UNVERIFIED AND CONTRADICTED, DO NOT USE: CNBC reports Reza Amiri Moghadam, Iran's ambassador to Islamabad, told AP on Saturday that Iran is prepared to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the US lifts its naval blockade, but that Washington rebuffed the proposal — and that "Later in the day, Iranian state media denied the report."
